title: Completion units and bounded domains of a compactification projection
statement: Fix the finite-field datum, $\ell\ne p$, finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and reduction presentation $m$ [def-pur-conventions, def-pur-compactification-reduction-models]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$ between separated finite-type schemes over the datum, and $c$ a compactification. Choose normalized equivalence data on $X,c.Z,Y$ [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,O_E)$ and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,O_E)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], use the coordinates [def-pur-compactification-b-projection-data]. The exact innerUnit and sourceUnit maps are homomorphisms of isomorphisms $h:H\simeq D$ and $v:V\simeq S$. The completed objects $D,S,PM,PD$ lie in the integral finite-Tor constructible categories. The systems $rM,rK,rD,rS,F_\bullet rD,rPM,rPD$, the inner system tensor $f_\bullet^*rK\otimes rM$, the source tensor $rK\otimes F_\bullet rM$, and the compact-support image of the inner tensor are all normalized constructible. The actual open inverse factor is invertible, as are the pinned reconstruction components $b_M,b_D$. No projection compatibility equation or naturality assertion is part of this domain lemma.

source.place: Paragraphs (1)-(3), completeness, common bounds, quotient units and reconstruction invertibility

proof.text: Use ordinary ringed derived operations temporarily, writing $f_R^*$ for ordinary pullback, $H=M\otimes^Lf_R^*K$, $V=PM\otimes^LK$, and $U=PH$. By [det-lem-int-tensor-pullback] and [det-lem-int-tensor-product], $f_R^*K,H$ are derived-complete bounded constructible. By [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower], $PM,PH$ are derived-complete bounded constructible; hence so is $V$ by the tensor theorem. Their reduction systems are normalized by [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. For uniform finite-Tor bounds, pullback preserves a finite interval by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], tensor adds the two intervals by [lem-sf-tensor-ctf], and compact support widens the interval by $2d$ by the direct-image theorem. Thus $r_XM,r_YK,r_XH,r_YV,r_YU$ have the common bounds required below. The finite statements apply to $O/\ell^n=O/\varpi^{en}$, with no unramifiedness assumption.

source.place: Paragraphs (1)-(3), ordinary constructible operations and uniform finite-level bounds

proof.text: The ordinary/complete identifications are canonical, not arbitrary object isomorphisms. Write $u_A:A\to LrA$ and $e_C:rLC\to C$ for the actual reduction/limit adjunction. For an ordinary tensor $A\otimes^LB$ occurring here, [lem-sp-reduction-derived-monoidal-tower] gives $\mu:r(A\otimes^LB)\simeq rA\otimes^LrB$, on flat-term representatives by $(a\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto(a\otimes1)\otimes(b\otimes c)$. The map $L(\mu)u_{A\otimes B}$ identifies this tensor with the completed tensor defined in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]; it is invertible by Step 1 and [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. The pullback identification is the map $c_K$ of [det-lem-int-tensor-pullback]. Consequently $H\simeq M\widehat\otimes^LLf^*K$ and $V\simeq PM\widehat\otimes^LK$. The triangle identity $e_{rA}r(u_A)=1$, together with naturality of $e$, shows that reducing these identifications gives exactly the comparisons from the one quotient diagram, tensor balancing and the reconstruction counit. These are the specified simultaneous reduction coordinates in the question.

source.place: Paragraph (3), normalization of tensor and pullback by quotient augmentations

proof.text: For $N=M,H$, the comparison needed for projection descent is the specified $b_N$. To check its normalization, $j$ is quasi-compact by [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target], since $p_cj=f$ is finite type and $p_c$ is proper, hence quasi-separated. The schemes in $c$ are qcqs. Apply [lem-sp-complete-compactification-limit-realization]: its $\alpha_{c,N}:PN\simeq L_YF_\bullet r_XN$ is $P(u_N)$ followed by the open/limit, proper/limit and scalar-restriction comparisons, all on strict systems. Its reduction transpose is $e_{F_\bullet r_XN}r_Y(\alpha_{c,N})$. The comparison in [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower](2), and hence the $b_N$ fixed in [lem-sp-integral-reconstruction-comparisons], uses exactly this compactification comparison and reconstruction counit. Thus these are the same entire-system map $b_N$, with no change of normalization or choice of evaluated isomorphisms.

source.place: Paragraph (2), the canonical compactification/limit map and its reduction transpose

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-tower-compact-support-projection-formula] with $C_\bullet=r_XM$, $B_\bullet=r_YK$, and the same $c$. Step 1 verifies its uniform constructible finite-Tor hypotheses. It says separately that the proper counit projection and the open unit projection are invertible, and specifies them as actual system maps. Their composite, with the inverse open factor, is the system projection $\theta:F_\bullet r_XM\otimes^Lr_YK\to F_\bullet(r_XM\otimes^Lf_\bullet^*r_YK)$ used below. This verifies both invertibility assumptions of [lem-sp-complete-projection-mate-descent]; its other assumptions are the completeness and bounded-below reductions of $M,K,H,U,V$ from Step 1 and the normalized limit/reconstruction comparisons from Step 4.

source.place: Paragraph (3), the two tower projection factors and the hypotheses of projection descent

proof.text: Transport domain membership along the actual tensor, pullback and reconstruction isomorphisms to obtain each displayed coefficient-first system domain. These isomorphisms preserve common cohomological and Tor bounds and all transitions.
